review.summary:
Attempt 4 of the phase-19 typed-preservation chunk closes all four attempt-3 low findings with executed evidence and adds no regressions I can find.

Documentation drift is fixed and now machine-bound. docs/CI.md:4 states 49 required jobs, docs/RELEASE.md:10 states the 48-job Rust feature/compiler matrix and :17 the terminal 49-job CI, and tools/check_phase.py:488 says 48-job. The new guard tools/test_ci.py:110-121 derives rust_jobs = len(flow_list("toolchain")) * len(flow_list("features")) and total = rust_jobs + 1 from .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:89-90, asserts "Its 49 required jobs" appears in docs/CI.md, and regex-binds both RELEASE.md numbers while deliberately excluding historical text after "The prior [0.2.0 receipt]". I counted ci.yml:90 by hand: 24 feature sets x 2 toolchains + 1 contracts job = 49, and scripts/check-rust.py:20-29 defines exactly those 24 keys, with json-unification restored to the historical bare core and red-team-json-unification added. That test executed: docs/checks/phase-19-python-preflight.json records `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p test_*.py -v` -> 308 tests, OK, exit 0, at source_sha256 4f814fd7..., and its stderr contains test_current_documented_job_counts_match_the_configured_matrix. It also runs in CI, because ci.yml:72 invokes `--phase 17 --verification-only --contracts-only` and commands_for(17) includes the full test_*.py discovery.

Both response modes are now exercised. tools/g25_fixtures.py:457 and :497 emit `projection_roundtrip(name, value, mode)` and `projection_state(name, field, value, mode)`, and the three generated sweeps loop [Mode::Response, Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults] at g25_response_compatibility.rs:366, :1027 and :1063. assert_projection_policy:346-356 is the stronger form of the check: it compares the typed roundtrip to `validation::parse(schema, input, mode)` output in both modes and additionally asserts byte-identity with the input in ResponseWithoutDefaults, so default injection around a vendor-added field cannot silently alter or drop a value. The 55-row x 6-shape fallback matrix, the 55-field typed-state/nullability sweep and the all-model u128 sweep all run in both modes now.

The supplementary all-features gap is closed rather than merely annotated: docs/checks/phase-19-rust-1.99.0-all-round4.json is passed true at rustInputsSha256 1bba8d14..., the same Rust input state as all five gate receipts, and records union_nested_projection..., every_projection_model_preserves_large_unknown_numbers_through_public_parse, every_vendor_projection_populates_typed_values_and_preserves_nullability and g25_typed_reads_preserve_opaque_ids_dates_and_unknown_enum_values as ok. The superseded round2 and round3 receipts are explicitly scoped in docs/phase-status.json:3967-3977, and the chunk scope list at :3874-3885 now names all ten changed artifacts.

The codec itself is unchanged and correct. tools/generate_models.py:472 raises if a vendor projection is not optional; :489 decodes each projection via crate::json_decode::from_value and re-inserts the untouched wire value on failure; :495 decodes the baseline remainder through the same boundary with a redacted error; :498 omits projection wires from KNOWN so baseline collisions stay hard errors; :505 suppresses the raw entry only when the typed field is set. generated.rs:8116-8221 matches that emission exactly for AttackOutput, and the file contains exactly 25 `baseline response model mismatch` impls matching the 25 rustType values in projections.json; `generate_models.py --check` and `g25_fixtures.py --check` both passed, so the committed Rust arms provably match the generator. Transport-level coverage is real: red_team_contracts.rs:2478-2515 drives list_attacks and get_target_profile_error_logs through the public client and Wire in both response modes with job-1/p-1/map-1, both reported timestamp forms, novel enum values and a 128-bit number, asserting the response equals the fixture exactly.

What remains is test fidelity and secondary bookkeeping, not product defects. The 46-root, 15,658-case operation sweep still decodes through `serde_json::from_value` (g25_response_compatibility.rs:47-50) rather than the SDK's production decoder, so the largest preservation sweep does not bind crate::json_decode; 10 of the 55 `conforming` witnesses are empty containers; docs/CI.md:152 and the check_phase.py docstring counts are correct but unbound; and docs/CI.md:11 still describes the CI gate as the Phase 12 gate while ci.yml:72 runs phase 17. No blocker, high or medium finding.

findings.description: The largest preservation sweep does not use the SDK's production decoder. `typed<T>` at :47-50 calls `serde_json::from_value` and is the body of every generated operation arm in `roundtrip` (:138-280), which `every_vendor_response_root_matches_independent_compatibility_outcomes` invokes at :131 for 46 roots x 15,658 cases x 2 response modes. Production decoding is `support::parse` -> `crate::json_decode::from_value` (crates/scm-sdk/src/models/support.rs:106-116), which differs from serde_json's decoder exactly under `serde_json/arbitrary_precision` for 128-bit numeric tokens, reserved protocol keys and Content-buffered untagged/flatten paths (crates/scm-sdk/src/json_decode.rs:1-12, :280-311). The projection arms were migrated to the production boundary in attempt 3, but the operation arms were not, so the sweep that covers all 46 roots could pass while the production path failed. The corpus values are all representable, so no current divergence is demonstrated; this is a fidelity gap, not an observed defect. Note the mechanical obstacle: `crate::json_decode::from_value` is pub(crate), and several operation roots are arrays or unconstrained JSON with no `::parse` associated function.
findings.required_fix: Route the generated operation arms through the production decode boundary: emit `<Type>::parse(value, mode)` in tools/g25_fixtures.py:441 for roots whose Rust type exposes `parse`, and for array/JsonValue roots either add a small public or `#[doc(hidden)]` decode entry point the integration test can call, or assert those roots separately and document them as decoder-exempt. Then re-run scripts/check-rust.py for red-team and red-team-json-unification on 1.89.0 and 1.99.0.

findings.description: Ten of the 55 `conforming` witnesses are empty containers, so for those fields the 'typed projection populates a value' assertion proves only that an empty object decodes. tools/g25_fixtures.py:292-297 builds an object witness from non-optional properties only, and :305-306 returns `{}` for every ZodRecord, so for example AttackDetailResponse.threat_details (projections.json:41) has `"conforming": {}`. crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:1033-1038 then asserts only state == "value" for that witness; the nested structure of the typed projection is never decoded. The other 45 rows carry real content, and the null/wrong-type/nested-extra matrix at :359-382 still covers all 55, so this narrows witness strength rather than leaving a field untested.
findings.required_fix: Strengthen the witness generator in tools/g25_fixtures.py:292-306 to populate at least one optional property (and at least one record entry) when the required-property projection would otherwise be empty, regenerate contracts/compatibility/g25/projections.json and the Rust arms, and re-run the red-team feature checks on both compilers.

findings.description: Two further job-count statements remain unbound by the new guard. docs/CI.md:152 states 'The independent 48-job Rust matrix continues to test every supported feature selection on both compilers' and tools/check_phase.py:488 documents 'the independent 48-job Rust matrix'. Both are currently correct (24 features x 2 toolchains = 48), but tools/test_ci.py:110-121 binds only the 'Its {total} required jobs' sentence in docs/CI.md and the two docs/RELEASE.md numbers, so these two can drift silently the next time the matrix changes, which is precisely the failure mode attempt 3 reported.
findings.required_fix: Extend tools/test_ci.py:110-121 to also assert the rust_jobs figure in the docs/CI.md 'Scripts run by the current contracts gate' section and in the tools/check_phase.py ci_commands_for docstring, so every present-tense count is derived from flow_list("toolchain") x flow_list("features").

findings.description: Stale gate identification in a file this chunk edited. docs/CI.md:11 states 'CI now executes the vendor-delivery Phase 12 gate, whose invocation and current script inventory are enforced by tools/test_ci.py', while .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:72 runs `python3 tools/check_phase.py --phase 17 --verification-only --contracts-only` and docs/CI.md:105 correctly describes that phase-17 contracts job. tools/test_ci.py:54-55 only requires the substring '--phase 17' to appear somewhere in the document, so the contradictory prose at :11 passes. This predates the chunk, but docs/CI.md is part of this round's delta and the surrounding sentence is present tense.
findings.required_fix: Update docs/CI.md:11-13 to name the Phase 17 contracts gate that ci.yml:72 actually invokes, keeping the Phase 8/12/92 references explicitly historical.

findings.description: The union-nested regression runs in only one response mode. `union_nested_projection_preserves_large_numbers_without_falling_back_to_unknown` at :1070-1091 calls `StreamDetailResponse::parse(input, Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults)` once, while every other projection sweep in the file was parameterized over both modes in this round. Default injection into or around the untagged StreamDetailResponseGoal union carrying a 128-bit number is therefore unexercised, which is the one place where the Content-buffer hazard and default application interact.
findings.required_fix: Wrap the body of crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:1085-1090 in `for mode in [Mode::Response, Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults]`, comparing against `validation::parse` output in the defaults-enabled mode as assert_projection_policy does, and re-run the red-team-json-unification checks on both compilers.

evidence: Gate completeness: docs/reviews/phase-19-chunk-typed-preservation-attempt-04.checks.json records source_sha256 4f814fd7e949e4442189a95879476ce682f8a52258c05b718572b1cbce3c1068, source_unchanged true, passed true, checked_at 2026-10-19T04:34:00.667215+00:00, and exactly 26 commands, every one exit_code 0 and timeout false. That list matches tools/check_phase.py:70-91 item for item, including the five scripts/check-rust.py runs (1.89.0 and 1.99.0 red-team, 1.99.0 json-unification, 1.89.0 and 1.99.0 red-team-json-unification). docs/checks/phase-19.json carries the identical source hash and checked_at, so the gate report and the chunk evidence are one execution.

Attempt-3 finding 1 closed and bound: docs/CI.md:4 'Its 49 required jobs', docs/RELEASE.md:10 '48-job Rust feature/compiler matrix', :17 'terminal 49-job CI', tools/check_phase.py:488 'independent 48-job Rust matrix'. tools/test_ci.py:110-121 computes rust_jobs = len(flow_list("toolchain")) * len(flow_list("features")), asserts f'Its {rust_jobs+1} required jobs' is in docs/CI.md, and regex-binds both RELEASE.md numbers after truncating the historical tail at 'The prior [0.2.0 receipt]'. I counted .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:90 by hand (24 feature sets) and scripts/check-rust.py:20-29 (24 keys), giving 24 x 2 + 1 = 49.

That guard actually executed at the reviewed source: docs/checks/phase-19-python-preflight.json records the full `python3 -m unittest discover -s tools -p test_*.py -v` with exit_code 0, 'Ran 308 tests', 'OK (', source_sha256 4f814fd7... and source_unchanged true, and its stderr names test_current_documented_job_counts_match_the_configured_matrix. It is also reachable in CI: .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:72 runs `--phase 17 --verification-only --contracts-only` and tools/check_phase.py commands_for(17):104 includes the full test_*.py discovery, which ci_commands_for only filters for native scripts.

Attempt-3 finding 2 closed: tools/g25_fixtures.py:457 emits `<Name>::parse(value,mode)` arms and :497 emits `projection_state(name,field,value,mode)`; crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:366, :1027 and :1063 each loop [Mode::Response, Mode::ResponseWithoutDefaults]. assert_projection_policy:346-356 asserts the typed roundtrip equals `validation::parse(schema, input, mode)` in both modes and additionally equals the raw input in ResponseWithoutDefaults, so defaults-enabled behavior around every one of the 55 added fields is now checked rather than skipped.

Attempt-3 finding 3 closed with a re-run, not just a note: docs/checks/phase-19-rust-1.99.0-all-round4.json is passed true at rustInputsSha256 1bba8d14e40eb886e2a7cb933628e6874aee497ab31c7f1d70ffe1501fff8eab, the same value carried by all five gate receipts (1.89.0/1.99.0 red-team, 1.99.0 json-unification, 1.89.0/1.99.0 red-team-json-unification). The superseded all-round2 (4662feb3...) and the docs/checks/phase-19-round3/ directory (aaa4045a...) are explicitly scoped in docs/phase-status.json:3967-3977.

Executed test names, not prose: docs/checks/phase-19-rust-1.89.0-red-team-json-unification.json records `test typed_replacement_wins_projection_fallback_and_baseline_collisions_still_fail ... ok`, `test union_nested_projection_preserves_large_numbers_without_falling_back_to_unknown ... ok`, `test projection_models_preserve_large_numbers_through_the_sdk_json_boundary ... ok`, `test every_projection_model_preserves_large_unknown_numbers_through_public_parse ... ok`, `test every_vendor_projection_populates_typed_values_and_preserves_nullability ... ok`, `test every_vendor_added_projection_preserves_absence_null_and_unrepresentable_values ... ok` and `test g25_typed_reads_preserve_opaque_ids_dates_and_unknown_enum_values ... ok`. The 1.99.0 counterpart and the all-features round4 receipt record the same set.

Codec correctness is generator-bound: tools/generate_models.py:472 raises 'Vendor response projections must remain optional'; :489 decodes each projection via crate::json_decode::from_value and re-inserts the untouched wire value on error; :495 decodes the baseline remainder through the same boundary with a redacted custom error; :498 builds KNOWN from non-projection wires only; :505 skips the raw entry only when the typed field is set. crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs:8116-8221 is exactly that emission for AttackOutput (five projections removed, BaselineWire over the ten baseline fields plus flattened extensions), and the file contains exactly 25 'baseline response model mismatch' impls matching the 25 rustType values in contracts/compatibility/g25/projections.json. `tools/generate_models.py --check` -> {"checked": true, "outputs": 16, "graphNodes": 13018} and `tools/g25_fixtures.py --check` -> {"roots": 46, "mutations": 15658, "formats": 184, "enums": 138, "typedProjectionFields": 55} both passed, and g25_fixtures.py:527 raises 'G25 generated fixture/binding is stale' on any drift.

Serializer invariants are directly tested: crates/scm-sdk/tests/g25_response_compatibility.rs:466-487 shows an unrepresentable judge_reasoning leaves the typed field unset and roundtrips byte-identically, an explicit typed replacement wins and emits a single key, and an extension colliding with the baseline field `uuid` makes serialization fail. The decode boundary is the production one: crates/scm-sdk/src/models/support.rs:106-116 runs ensure_supported -> validation::parse -> crate::json_decode::from_value, and crates/scm-sdk/src/json_decode.rs:280-311 routes only 128-bit numeric tokens through the public reader to avoid Serde's ContentVisitor limitation.

Public transport coverage exists for the reported cases: crates/scm-sdk/tests/red_team_contracts.rs:2478-2515 loops without_defaults in [false, true] over RedTeamReportsClient::list_attacks and RedTeamClient::get_target_profile_error_logs, injecting a 128-bit future_number, job-1/p-1/map-1, FUTURE_SUB_CATEGORY/FUTURE_CATEGORY/FUTURE_STATUS, '2026-01-05 00:00:00' and '2026-01-05T00:00:00.123456', then asserts the returned value equals case["responseBody"] exactly with wire.count() == 1.

Chunk scope and governance are now honest about the delta: docs/phase-status.json:3874-3885 lists all ten artifacts (generate_models.py, generated.rs, both Rust test files, g25_fixtures.py, projections.json, check-rust.py, ci.yml, test_ci.py, check_phase.py), matching the prompt, and :3963-3965 records the round-3 consolidation including 'generated projection tests cover both response modes' and the CI/doc binding. docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:15 and :19 document the projection fallback, the typed-replacement precedence, the retained baseline-collision error and the bounded value copy, and :197 still states the 17 airs-cli-rs loopback tests were not executed here.
limitations: Bash is unavailable in this session, so I could not recompute the reviewed source SHA256 (4f814fd7...), the attempt-4 checks-file SHA256 (895b76cb...), any rustInputsSha256, or the casesSha256 corpus binding, and I could not re-execute any command. I assessed the recorded commands, exit codes, stdout/stderr, durations and hashes as records. They are internally consistent, match tools/check_phase.py:70-91 exactly, share one rustInputs hash across all five gate receipts plus the round4 all-features receipt, and carry plausible wall-clock times, but they are verified as records rather than by re-running them.

I verified the 49-job arithmetic by hand-counting .forgejo/workflows/ci.yml:90 (24 entries) and the FEATURES keys in scripts/check-rust.py:20-29 (24 keys); the executed preflight receipt is my evidence that tools/test_ci.py:108 and :110-121 passed, since I could not run them.

crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs is very large. I read the AttackOutput projection impl in full and relied on grep counts (25 'baseline response model mismatch' impls, 25 distinct rustType values in projections.json) plus the passing `generate_models.py --check` and `g25_fixtures.py --check` rather than reading all 25 impls.

docs/phase-status.json changed during this review: its phase-19 scope_evidence gained 'docs/checks/phase-19-rust-1.99.0-all-round4.json' at line 3779 after my first read, and the entry is absent from the scope list supplied in my prompt. This does not invalidate the reviewed source hash, because tools/review_phase.py:15-16 excludes docs/phase-status.json, docs/reviews/ and docs/checks/ from the fingerprint by design, but it means bookkeeping files are not covered by the 4f814fd7 hash and I evaluated them at the state I observed.

I could not diff against the published 0.2.1 source, so my conclusion that no existing public projection field type changed rests on the fail-closed optionality guard at tools/generate_models.py:472-473, the generator check, and the unchanged model-additions contract, not on a byte comparison with the published crate.

Per the scoping instruction I reviewed the typed-preservation chunk and its ten declared artifacts in depth and did not re-audit the validation-policy or regression-and-governance chunks, phase 18's accepted plan and audit, the 15,658 independent Zod outcomes, or historical release infrastructure. Later-phase deliverables (phase-20 qualification, publication, terminal CI) are out of scope.

Live service acceptance and consumer adoption are unverified and unclaimed. The 17 reported airs-cli-rs loopback failures live on a host this checkout cannot reach, and the 49-job CI matrix has no terminal run receipt yet; both are explicitly deferred.

I read no credential or tenant-registration material and stayed inside this repository; I inspected docs/checks/phase-19-private-material.json only through the gate record's stdout ({"receiptFresh": true, "privateScanReexecuted": false, "gitVisibleFilesChecked": 1673}).
